messages:
vivian: Quick heads-up: merged a docs + SDK update today that changes the default locale/zone handling for structured date parsing in sdk-json v2.2.0. Not a model change, but it can affect timestamp normalization in apps that assume UTC.
omar: short TL;DR?
vivian: Previously the SDK parsed ambiguous dates without a timezone and assumed UTC. Now it derives the default timezone from the `REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ` env or the system locale if unset. This helps i18n use-cases but can shift normalized timestamps if you relied on implicit UTC.
jin: is this considered breaking?
vivian: It's a behavioral change shipped in a minor release (2.2.0). We treat it as a compatibility-impacting change for edge-cases. Docs updated with migration steps and a tiny compatibility shim.
docs-bot: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1012 "SDK JSON: default timezone and locale handling for date parsing". Added examples, migration checklist, and CLI shim.
i18n-bot: Scan: 27 repos use ambiguous date strings (e.g., "2024-03-15 12:00") and may see offsets. See internal report at /internal/i18n/reports/date-ambiguous-2024-03.csv (private).
support: we'll need a blurb for customer-facing release notes — a short explanation and recommended action.
jin: what's the recommended immediate action for infra/CIs?
vivian: 1) Grep for date strings without timezone in config/templates. 2) If you need old UTC behavior, set REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ=UTC in env or pin to sdk-json==2.1.9. 3) Run our CLI shim to annotate ambiguous dates:```bash
# annotate ambiguous dates in project templates
redwood-cli run annotate-dates --format ambiguous --fix --backup
# or enforce legacy behavior:
export REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ=UTC
pip install redwood-sdk-json==2.1.9
``` 
omar: timeline for fully removing legacy pin/flags?
vivian: We'll keep legacy pinning guidance and the CLI shim for 60 days. After that we'll require explicit timezone on ambiguous dates. Deprecation notice added to changelog: "legacy UTC fallback removed in 60 days".
jin: docs change looks good. Can we add a small snippet showing how to make parsing explicit in code?
docs-bot: added snippet in PR showing Date.parse(dateStr, {timezone: 'UTC'}) and Date.parse(dateStr, {locale: 'en-GB'}) for clarity.
support: i'll draft the release note: "Behavioral change: SDK now defaults to REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ or system locale when parsing ambiguous dates. If your app assumed implicit UTC, set REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ=UTC or pin to 2.1.9 until you migrate." Would also like a one-liner for the customer template.
jin: thanks. i'll post a short announcement in #eng and #product with links to the PR and the checklist.
ivian: (typo) vivian: also: if anyone needs more than 60 days, DM me and we can arrange a temporary flag. :sparkles:
vivian: final checklist for teams: 1) scan templates/configs for ambiguous dates, 2) apply shim or set REDWOOD_DEFAULT_TZ, 3) run integration tests, 4) remove legacy pin after migration.
